note:
<hideFromJabsMenu>
found in a chest
in the first pass through
the salt mines
description:
A flux drive that is a deep ruby red, kinda like an 🍎.
Unlocks the "Bloody Exchange" difficulty layer.

name: Flux Drive: Saffron
note:
<hideFromJabsMenu>
found behind a bomb wall
in Lakeside Road
in the Meandering Way
description:
A flux drive that is a vibrant orange, like an 🍊.
Unlocks the "Omniplating" difficulty layer.

name: Flux Drive: Lemon
note:
<hideFromJabsMenu>
found in a chest
in the Highwater Way
in the Northern Way
description:
A flux drive that is shockingly yellow, similar to a 🍋.
Unlocks the "Glass House" difficulty layer.

name: Flux Drive: Viridian
description:
A flux drive that bears an unusual resemblance to the color of 🌳.
Unlocks the "Wild Overgrowth" difficulty layer.

name: Flux Drive: Aqua
description:
A flux drive that is bright like a rushing 🌊.
Unlocks the "Redirection of Flow" difficulty layer.

name: Flux Drive: Royal
description:
A flux drive of regal authority, flaunting its royal blueness like a 👑.
Unlocks the "Limitless Energy" difficulty layer.

name: Flux Threadbooster
description:
Increases the number of threads available to the spacial flux engine.
Increases \C[1]Max Layer Points by 5\C[0].

name: Recipe Scrap
description:
A scrap of a recipe.
Turn these in for recipes to Yelena.

name: Blueprint Scrap
description:
A scrap of a blueprint.
Turn these in for blueprints to Viskra.

name: Pattern Scrap
description:
A scrap of a pattern.
Turn these in for patterns to Millie.

name: Formula Scrap
description:
A scrap of a formula.
Turn these in for formulas to Alice.

name: Alchemy Page
description:
A page torn from a legendary alchemist's journal.
Turn these in for formulas to Leo.

name: Philosopher's Stone
description:
The legendary stone of transmutation, whole at last.
Opens Material Mastery and Breakdown at alchemy stations.

name: Node Dust
description:
Faint glowing molecules that you breathed inadvertently.
Grants \C[3]100\C[0] node points to each ally.

name: Node Microgems
description:
Microscopic crystals that you stepped on inadvertently.
Grants \C[3]1000\C[0] node points to each ally.

name: Node Crystals
description:
Small crystalloids that you brushed against inadvertently.
Grants \C[3]5000\C[0] node points to each ally.

name: Node Geode
description:
Sizeable glowing geode of crystals that you bumped into inadvertently.
Grants \C[3]10000\C[0] node points to each ally.

name: Node Formations
description:
A collection of radiating geodes that you tripped over inadvertently.
Grants \C[3]25000\C[0] node points to each ally.

name: Node Stalactites
description:
A giant mass of vibrant crystalline spires you hit your head on inadvertently.
Grants \C[3]100000\C[0] node points to each ally.

name: Rouge Technodisk
description:
A reddish translucent and hyper-thin multi-part disk keycard that contains petabytes of encrypted information that open certain gates.
You found it in the Erocia Kingdom's Guard Office.

name: Bleu Technodisk
description:
A bluish translucent and hyper-thin multi-part disk keycard that contains petabytes of encrypted information that open certain gates.
This is not yet implemented.

name: Verte Technodisk
description:
A fragment of a greenish technodisk for opening gates.
This is not yet implemented.

name: RGB Technohypercube
description:
A cube of fissioned technodisks radiating colors that your eyes can't even perceive.
This is not yet implemented.

name: Technokey
description:
A key from the very top of the tower.
Opens the courtyard gate.

name: Avian Eggs
description:
The classic of classic, eggs from a bird.
You can use these for all sorts of fine cookery.

name: Bug Eggs
description:
They are wiggling, slimy, and extra tiny. These are quite possibly
the grossest thing you've carried around on purpose.

name: Froggo Eggs
description:
The eggs from a froggo are much like what you recall coming from regular frogs.
Tadpoles come from these if left unattended, so attend them!

name: Ghosty Eggs
description:
Did you think ghostys around here were the spirits of the dead?
They are living creatures just like you and me, but cute and spooky.

name: Lanky Tail
description:
A long, skinny tail that's more gristle than meat.
Low and slow is the only way this one is ever getting tender.

name: Beefy Tail
description:
Do not mistake the name for this being a thick and juicy tail.
There appears to be actual beef(!!!) or beef-like meat on this tail left.

name: Dargin Tail
description:
While the tail does have some sort of scales still attached, it is clear that you have
the means to penetrate the scales, so who cares? Itadakimasu!

name: Ripped Flank
description:
The flank of a beast that looks like its been ripped off-
probably with bare hands- from the animal it once resided on.

name: Bearcat Flank
description:
Bearcat meat is well-known for being terrible in flavor, gamey as all hell,
and like chewing through leather at any temp of cook.

name: Giga Flank
description:
A slab of flank so big it needs its own bag, carved off the biggest beasts around.
Premium cut. The beasts did not agree to this.

name: Boney Ribs
description:
Though the ribs and rib meat all look intact, the animal you
chose to destroy to get these ribs must've been nearly starved.

name: Lamia Ribs
description:
The ribs of a super long lamia.
As a result, there are a fuckton of them.

name: Ouroboros Ribs
description:
Eternally self-consuming ribs that make no sense.
Just accept that they are top-tier and probably used to JAFT some really nice things.

name: Flappy Wing
description:
A wing that is still flapping, despite you having removed it from its
original owner.

name: Double Wing
description:
A large wing that appears to be actually two wings that work
together to accomplish flight. This monster must've grown two wings from one joint.

name: Iridescent Wing
description:
A perfectly intact wing that sparkles all colors of the rainbow.
It smells faintly of potatoes.

name: Detached Eyeball
description:
The eye has been severed from its connective tissue that
is required for most uses, making this mostly useless.

name: Snooping Eyeball
description:
This eyeball does not appear to require a host, it floats about on its
own, but seems content to reside in your endless item sack.

name: Peerless Eyeball
description:
This eye clearly is able to see through not only you, but also through
your family and friends and probably walls and clothing.

name: Dried Blood
description:
Some kind of animal blood that has been dried for a while.
This is the result of a bit of rain loosening it so you can pick it up.

name: Virgin Blood
description:
Probably not from an actual virgin, but instead from one of those harpies
that are called "virgins" up in the mountains.

name: Blue Blood
description:
The finest of fine things across the land- blue blood.
Only the royalest of royals carry this blood.

name: Beast Heart
description:
The heart of your foes serves as a fine prize for their defeat.
There are probably other uses, beyond holding it proudly.

name: Hydro Heart
description:
A heart from the aquatic sort are strange and more core-like or something.
It is certainly pulsing still; you should probably store it while it still can exist outside of water.

name: Titan Heart
description:
Giant hearts are just massive and extremely heavy. Carrying more than one of these,
in your item sack no less, is a truly legendary feat to its own, nevermind defeating them for this.

name: Droopy Gelatin
description:
A sad little blob of gelatin that can barely hold its own shape.
Melt it into a stock and it'll set again once it cools.

name: Big Gelatin
description:
Slime monsters keep it all together with the power of science!
And also gelatin.

name: Oversized Gelatin
description:
A huge ass glob of gelatin probably carved from a kingly slime or something.
It strangely has no smell.

name: Colossus Gelatin
description:
Gelatin on a scale that should not be possible. It wobbles for a full minute after you set it down.
The finest gel a kitchen could ask for, assuming the kitchen can hold it.

name: Smelly Fish
description:
It appears to be a standard freshwater cod.
Unfortunately, it is well past its prime and will likely be questionable in taste when cooked.

name: Fresh Fish
description:
A giant bass that likely was found in some nearby river.
Its scales glisten in the sunlight- probably because its still wet.

name: Sparkling Fish
description:
When salmon are grown in saltwater, their skin gets tougher, but
the flesh tastes even more delicious.

name: Pristine Fish
description:
An entire tuna that has must've come from the ocean.
It is colossal, and a mystery how you are storing this in your item sack, much less likely multiples.

name: Red Pepper
description:
Though its called a pepper, the capsaicin is fairly low.
Even the most spice-sensitive can usually tolerate these.

name: Green Pepper
description:
A firm green pepper, picked before it ever had a chance to blush.
A little bitter, and it counts as a spice when a recipe wants one.

name: Heat Pepper
description:
A pepper that's warm to hold and a whole lot warmer to eat.
Counts as a spice, and then some.

name: Tingly Pepper
description:
A strange little pepper that leaves your lips buzzing for an hour.
Counts as a spice, if numbness is a flavor you're after.

name: Red Tomato
description:
A juicy and luscious tomato. Almost as versatile as a potato.
This can be used in all sorts of dishes.

name: Green Tomatillo
description:
A tart little tomatillo, still wearing its papery husk.
Bright, sour, and it counts as a fruit as well as a tomato.

name: Vine Tomato
description:
A cluster of tomatoes still clinging to the vine, smelling like summer.
Sweet enough to count as a fruit.

name: Crimson Tomato
description:
A deep crimson tomato, heavy and rich, the best the vine has to offer.
Is it a fruit or a vegetable? In this kitchen, both.

name: Bitter Vine
description:
A tough green vine torn off a carnivorous plant. It tastes exactly how it sounds.
Blanch it first. You'll thank yourself.

name: Poison Vine
description:
A vine off a man-eating plant, mildly toxic and a little too proud of it.
Cooking takes the edge off. Mostly.

name: Venom Vine
description:
A vine dripping with something that sizzles wherever it lands.
Cooked right, it's a delicacy. Cooked wrong, it's a story.

name: Death Vine
description:
A black vine from the deadliest man-eaters around. Handle with gloves. Two pairs.
Potent, prized, and absolutely not to be eaten raw.

name: Green Beans
description:
A pod of green beans, right off the vine.
These are great for adding texture and healthiness to your cuisine.

name: Round Beans
description:
Fat, round beans that go creamy when you cook them.
They can stand in for dairy, which is more than most beans can say.

name: Sugar Beans
description:
Beans with a natural sweetness, like candy that grew in a pod.
They can stand in for something sweet.

name: Scarlet Beans
description:
Bright red beans with a peppery bite.
They can stand in for a spice.

name: Sprouts
description:
A tangle of fresh sprouts, crunchy and very green.
They add a little life to whatever they get tossed into.

name: Fermented Sprouts
description:
Sprouts that have been left to ferment until they got pungent and funky.
They count as a fungus, for better or worse.

name: Sticky Sprouts
description:
Sprouts coated in a sweet, sticky sap that gets on absolutely everything.
They count as something sweet.

name: Sour Sprouts
description:
Sprouts with a sharp, sour tang, like they spent the night soaking in lemon.
They can stand in for citrus.

name: Lettuce
description:
Usually rather tasteless, but goes great with salads or
burgers due to the variance of texture.

name: Cabbage
description:
A dense, squeaky head of cabbage.
Shred it, stew it, or stuff it: it's game for anything.

name: Romaine
description:
Long, sturdy leaves of romaine, crisp from stem to tip.
Strong enough to wrap food in, so it works as a vessel.

name: Kale
description:
Curly, hearty kale that crisps up like a cracker in the oven.
It can stand in for bread. Don't knock it until you've tried it.

name: Leafy Greens
description:
A pile of leafy greens, petals, and other flora from the
bottom-most layer of a forest.

name: Bouncy Greens
description:
Unusually bouncy greens that you plucked from somewhere that you maybe shouldn't have.
Why are they bouncing? The world will never know.

name: Fine Greens
description: A mighty fine bunch of green greens.

name: Verdant Greens
description: The most greenest of green greenery that you ever did green.

name: Faerie Petal
description:
Most would believe these are the wings of a faerie, but really it
is a petal- literally a flake from their flesh.

name: Faerie Bud
description:
The bud of a faerie is basically just a premature bit of the faerie
that you really shouldn't be harvesting, you monster.

name: Faerie Blossom
description:
A beautiful blossom of a faerie. This only becomes available
when the faeries are at peak maturity.

name: Faerie Bouquet
description:
The bouquet is just five dozen faerie blossoms. Why in the world would
anyone need this?

name: Sad Carrot
description:
A limp, bendy carrot that has clearly given up on life.
Still sweet deep down, so it counts as something sweet. Cook it long enough and it might forgive you.

name: Orange Carrot
description:
A perfectly normal orange carrot. Nothing more, nothing less.
Sweet enough to count as something sweet.

name: Perky Carrot
description:
A bright, crunchy carrot standing at attention.
Its natural sugar lets it count as something sweet.

name: Happiness Carrot
description:
A carrot so cheerful it's practically smiling at you.
The sweetest carrot there is, and it knows it.

name: Yellow Onion
description:
Your basic yellow onion. Slightly sweet, but has a delicate
aroma that wafts deep into your happy little nostrils.

name: Ao Negi
description:
A long green Japanese onion, mild and grassy.
It counts as greens rather than an onion, so it won't fill an onion slot.

name: Shallot
description:
A small, elegant onion with a gentler bite.
Sweeter and subtler than its bigger cousins.

name: Tropea Onion
description:
A torpedo-shaped red onion, famous for being sweet enough to eat raw.
The finest onion the plant has to give.

name: Button Mushroom
description:
A generic mushroom with a cap that does mushroom things.
Grows up and looks gross, but can fill a variety of roles in food.

name: Whitecap Mushroom
description:
A mushroom with a bright white cap and a meaty bite.
Filling enough to count as a carb.

name: Shiitake Mushroom
description:
A dark, savory shiitake with a deep, woodsy smell.
It makes any broth taste like it simmered all day.

name: Maitake Mushroom
description:
A ruffled cluster of maitake, the dancing mushroom.
The finest fungus around, with the flavor to match.

name: Dry Coral
description:
Coral is brutally sharp when dry, and also brutally fragile.
So be careful!

name: River Coral
description:
The kind of coral you probably see kappas holding onto for some unknown reason.
They must miss their rivers, and here you are farming them for their home's keepsakes.

name: Layered Coral
description:
When coral grows a lot, it starts to layer upon itself.
It doesn't actually do this in any known science, but around here that seems to be the case.

name: Ancient Coral
description:
Coral older than any kingdom, hard as stone and twice as storied.
The deepest flavor the waters have to offer.

name: Eggplant
description:
A glossy purple eggplant that soaks up oil like a sponge.
Technically a fruit, so it counts as one.

name: Zucchini
description:
A long green zucchini, mild and mostly water.
It soaks up whatever flavor you throw at it.

name: Pumpkin
description:
A round orange pumpkin, heavy and sweet on the inside.
Dense enough to count as a carb.

name: Tofu
description:
Beans crushed to milk, heated, and set with mineral water until it holds a shape under its own weight.
The minerals do all of the work and the kitchen mostly just waits for them.

name: Brown Potato
description:
The most versatile of roots, the potato can be used for
so many things its an absolute atrocity you don't have 999 of them.

name: Gold Potato
description:
A golden-skinned potato with buttery yellow flesh.
It mashes smoother than any potato has a right to.

name: Big Ass Potato
description:
This is a big ass potato.
One of these could feed the whole party, with leftovers.

name: Is This Even Still A Potato
description:
It's shaped like a potato and smells like a potato, but it's the size of a small boulder.
The most potato a potato can possibly be.

name: Stale Nuts
description:
A handful of nuts that have seen better days.
Still crunchy. Mostly.

name: Peanuts
description:
Peanuts in the shell, which, strictly speaking, aren't even nuts.
Crunchy, cheap, and good in nearly everything.

name: Walnuts
description:
Wrinkly walnuts that look like tiny brains.
Rich, a little bitter, and very crunchy.

name: Hazelnuts
description:
Smooth, round hazelnuts with a toasty sweetness.
The finest nut on the tree, and the best friend chocolate ever had.

name: Macaroni
description:
Dough rolled, cut into stubby tubes, and boiled for the length of one argument.
Everything you have ever eaten off a noodle was waiting on somebody doing this first.

name: Linguini
description:
Rolled thinner and cut wider than macaroni, which changes everything about how sauce behaves on it.
Wheat specifically, because nothing else holds a long noodle together.

name: Soba
description:
Dark, nutty, and cooked in barely three minutes before being shocked cold.
Millet makes a noodle that tastes of something instead of merely carrying sauce.

name: Tortellini
description:
Squares of egg dough folded around whatever paste is to hand and a little cheese, one at a time, several hundred times.
Nobody has ever agreed on what belongs inside one, and the folding is the whole job regardless.

name: Oat
description:
A bundle of oats, hearty and humble.
Breakfast for horses and adventurers alike.

name: Wheat
description:
Golden wheat, the start of every loaf.
Grind it down and the possibilities are endless.

name: Rice
description:
The king of starches, can be used to make so many things that
its a miracle it exists everywhere you go.

name: Millet
description:
Tiny round grains of millet, nutty and quick to cook.
An ancient grain with plenty of tricks left in it.

name: Roll
description:
Mixed, left alone to do its own work, and baked under a lid until the tops go gold.
The single most useful thing anyone ever learned to do with wheat.

name: Loaf
description:
A full loaf rather than a roll, which means a longer rise and a real crust.
It keeps for days and is the backbone of half the bread recipes above.

name: Croissant
description:
Dough and butter folded through each other until there are more layers than anyone can count.
It has to be whole butter and never the clarified sort, because the water in it is what turns to steam and drives the layers apart.

name: Baguette
description:
Three ingredients, a long cold rise, and a crust that shatters loudly enough to turn heads.
The salt is doing structural work here and cutting it produces something sad and pale.

name: Grapes
description:
A bunch of grapes, plump and ready to burst.
Eat them fresh, or crush them into something stronger.

name: Raspberry
description:
Soft, fuzzy raspberries that stain everything they touch.
Tart, sweet, and made for desserts.

name: Currants
description:
Tiny, tart currants, red as rubies.
A little goes a long way.

name: Elderberry
description:
Dark elderberries in a drooping cluster.
Never eat them raw. Cooked, they're wonderful.

name: Banana
description:
A ripe yellow banana, sweet and soft.
Nature's own snack, wrapper included.

name: Coconut
description:
One of the only fruits that appear to grow in this land.
Fortunately, it can be used for both its milk, and its flesh.

name: Mango
description:
A juicy golden mango that runs down your arm the moment you bite it.
The sweetest thing the palms have to offer.

name: Papaya
description:
A long orange papaya packed with little black seeds.
Mellow, musky, and very tropical.

name: Lemon
description:
A golden yellow lemon, almost bursting with juice.
Though, you probably want to use the juice sparingly, its very tart.

name: Orange
description:
A juicy orange, sweet with just a little tang.
Easy to peel and easier to eat.

name: Pomelo
description:
A pomelo the size of your head, with a rind as thick as a mattress.
Sweet, mild, and worth all the peeling.

name: Yuzu
description:
A knobbly little yuzu with a fragrance like nothing else.
The most prized citrus in any kitchen.

name: Apple
description:
A crisp red apple.
Keeps the healer away, and goes in nearly every dessert.

name: Pear
description:
A soft, fragrant pear, ripe at the bottom first.
Gentle, sweet, and a little grainy.

name: Cherry
description:
A pair of glossy cherries joined at the stem.
Sweet, tart, and lovely on top of anything.

name: Plum
description:
A dusky purple plum, sweet flesh under a tart skin.
Delicious fresh, even better baked.

name: Melon
description:
A plain melon, hard rind outside and sweet flesh within.
Refreshing on a hot day, which is most days somewhere.

name: Watermelon
description:
A big striped watermelon, sloshing with juice.
Mostly water, entirely refreshing.

name: Canteloupe
description:
A netted rind hiding sweet, fragrant orange flesh.
Best served cold, in big wedges.

name: Honeydew
description:
A pale green honeydew, as honey-sweet as the name promises.
The finest melon on the vine.

name: Cheddar
description:
Curdled with acid, cut, stacked and pressed, then left alone for far longer than feels reasonable.
The first cheese anybody learns and the one they never stop making.

name: Brie
description:
Surface-ripened until a bloom forms and the inside goes to liquid underneath it.
Deliberately and carefully mouldy, which is a thing the roster evidently already knew.

name: Gouda
description:
A wheel of gouda, mild and creamy under a waxy rind.
Cheese counts as a fungus too; those cultures had to come from somewhere.

name: Parmesan
description:
Pressed hard, salted heavily, and then aged for longer than any other item in this lane.
It is the only cheese here that is genuinely a long-term investment.

name: Malk
description:
The source from which this white viscous liquid comes from is yet to be determined.
However, it does appear to function identically to milk in a cooking context.

name: Moo Juice
description:
Fresh moo juice, straight from something that moos. Probably.
Creamy, and it counts as a liquid.

name: Bug Juice
description:
A milky juice wrung out of bugs. Don't think too hard about how.
Rich, creamy, and it counts as a liquid.

name: Dragon Juice
description:
Dragon milk, warm and faintly smoky.
The richest dairy in the land, and a liquid as well.

name: Cream
description:
Left cold and undisturbed until the fat rises far enough to be skimmed off the top.
It is the least active recipe in this entire document and it still counts as cooking.

name: Thicc Cream
description:
Reduced over low heat until it is half the volume and twice the opinion.
Moo juice specifically, because the thinner milks simply refuse to cooperate.

name: Kream
description:
Whipped with sugar until it stiffens into something that holds a shape indefinitely.
The deliberate misspelling is the roster's problem and not this recipe's.

name: Volatile Cuhream
description:
Held just above freezing while something in the dragon milk refuses to settle.
It is stable for as long as it is cold and for no longer than that.

name: Creamed Cream
description:
Cream beaten past whipped, past stiff, and out the other side until it breaks into fat and liquid.
The moment it turns is unmistakable and slightly alarming the first time.

name: Refined Butter
description:
Melted, skimmed, and the clear fat poured carefully off the solids beneath.
It keeps almost forever and burns at a far higher heat, which is the entire point of the exercise.

name: Fat Paste
description:
Clarified butter beaten back together with cream into something spreadable and obscene.
It is not a good idea and it has never claimed to be one.

name: Devil Slick
description:
Rendered down with dragon milk until it goes dark, thin and faintly hot to the touch.
It fries harder than anything else in the kitchen and it browns things it was not aimed at.

name: Basic Yogert
description:
A plain tub of yogert. It's like yogurt, but basic.
Those live cultures let it count as a fungus.

name: Whipped Yogy
description:
Beaten with a little milk until it loosens and goes airy under the whisk.
Officially a fungus, which the roster insists upon and nobody wants to think about.

name: Velvet Yoggert
description:
Cultured slowly at a temperature that somebody has to physically sit and watch.
The reward is a texture that coats a spoon and declines to run off it.

name: Liquigurt
description:
Thinned until it can be drunk rather than spooned, and then thinned slightly further.
Somewhere between a yogurt and a beverage, and legally recognised as neither.

name: Cane Sugar
description:
Coarse sugar pressed out of sugar cane.
The sweet foundation under every dessert.

name: Syrup
description:
Sugar and water held at a boil until it thickens and threads off the back of a spoon.
It is the base of nearly every sweet thing that follows and it takes four minutes.

name: Rock Candy
description:
Supersaturated syrup left with a string in it for a week while crystals grow unattended.
The only recipe in this document where waiting is the entire method.

name: Powdered Sugar
description:
Ground to dust with a little grain worked in to stop it clumping in the damp.
It gets on everything within reach and stays there for days.

name: Leftover Slime
description:
This slime is pretty gross. It was leftover from one of the
countless slime monsters you've slain. Still sorta jiggly, though.

name: Slimy Slime
description:
The ways in english of saying "this is gross" are countless.
But this slime is downright nasty, offending all 8 of your senses.

name: Putrid Slime
description:
The power of smell offends you in ways you didn't think were possible.
This slime is both rancid to look at and smell- it is a mystery why you carry it still.

name: Archaic Slime
description:
Slime from an age long forgotten, preserved perfectly in its own goo.
The sweetest slime there is, aged like a fine wine.

name: Cacao
description:
A pod of raw cacao beans, bitter and earthy.
The very beginning of chocolate.

name: Burgundy Cacao
description:
Deep red cacao beans with a fruity, wine-like note.
They make a chocolate with some sophistication.

name: Double Dark Cacao
description:
Cacao beans so dark they're nearly black, and then darker still.
Intensely bitter, intensely good.

name: Black Cacao
description:
Pitch-black cacao, the rarest pod the tree produces.
The chocolate it makes is the stuff of legend.

name: Gummy Rings
description:
Slime cooked down with sugar, poured into moulds, and set cold until it bounces.
Nobody eating these wants to hear where the slime originally came from.

name: Earthen Circle
description:
Set into dark rings with something bitter and rooty worked all the way through.
A sweet that tastes of soil on purpose, and it has defenders.

name: Blazing Spiral
description:
Sugar cooked with enough chilli that the heat arrives second and then stays third.
The spiral shape is traditional and nobody remembers why.

name: Minty Dots
description:
Crushed candy set with mint into dots small enough to eat by the handful.
Overdo the mint and you have manufactured a medicine instead.

name: Box
description:
Not everything should rest directly in your infinite bag of holding. For those
cases, you should consider putting them in a container such as this.

name: Glass
description:
A clean drinking glass.
A vessel for anything you'd rather sip than chew.

name: Skewer
description:
A long, sharp stick for threading food onto.
A vessel, structurally speaking.

name: Tray
description:
A flat serving tray.
A vessel for presenting food with a little dignity.

name: Earthy Herbs
description:
A bundle of some of earthy, savory-smelling herbs.
Adding these to your dishes will surely add the umami you seek!

name: Minty Herbs
description:
A bundle of some of fresh and crisp-smelling herbs.
Adding these to your dishes will surely add the freshness you seek!

name: Spicy Herbs
description:
A bundle of some of fiery, and spicy-smelling herbs.
Adding these to your dishes will surely add the lava you seek!

name: Wispy Herbs
description:
A bundle of some of light and airy-smelling herbs.
Adding these to your dishes will surely add the whimsy you seek!

name: Water
description: Your basic in H2O, bottled up for your RPG convenience.

name: Distilled Water
description:
Boiled, caught as steam, and let fall back cold into a second vessel.
It tastes of absolutely nothing at all, which is the entire specification.

name: Mineral Water
description:
Water held against coral until it takes up the minerals and goes faintly hard across the tongue.
The only good reason to carry coral, and the kitchen is quietly relieved to have found one.

name: Pure Water
description:
Frozen slowly, so that everything which is not water is pushed out ahead of the advancing ice.
What remains when it melts is the cleanest thing in the game.

name: Salt
description:
Plain old salt.
The one spice every recipe secretly wants.

name: Cumin
description:
Warm, earthy cumin seeds.
One pinch and the whole camp smells like dinner.

name: Garlic
description:
A whole head of garlic, pungent and papery.
It counts as a spice. Rumor says vampires hate it.

name: Nutmeg
description:
A hard little nutmeg seed, best grated fresh.
A warm, sweet spice for desserts and creamy things.

name: Neutral Oil
description: The oil is well-refined and works wonders for searing all sorts of goods.

name: Meaty Oil
description:
Fat rendered out of trimmings over the lowest possible heat and strained clean.
It carries the animal into everything it touches, which is either the whole point or the whole problem.

name: Fresh Oil
description:
Greens crushed and pressed until they weep something violently green and grassy.
It tastes of the field it came out of and it does not keep for long.

name: Dense Oil
description:
Nuts crushed under weight until the oil runs and separates out.
Heavier and slower-moving than any other oil here, and it fries hotter than all of them.

name: Fruity Oil
description:
Pressed cold so that nothing in the fruit gets a chance to cook.
Cloudy, green-gold, and best used somewhere it will never be heated.

name: White Oil
description:
Butter melted and held until the solids drop away and the fat above runs clear and pale.
The most refined thing in the pantry and the most forgiving thing to cook with.

name: Candy Oil
description:
Sugar and fat cooked together until they emulsify into something glossy and faintly wrong.
Used only in desserts, and only by people who know exactly what they are doing.

name: Sea Salt
description:
Mineral water boiled away to nothing across a full day, until all that is left in the pan is what the coral put into it, dried into
flakes you can hear break. A handful costs a day and a great deal of fuel, which is why the coarse stuff still sells by the sack.

name: Scrambies
description:
The default breakfast of anyone who woke up in a tent.
Whisked hard, cooked fast, and seasoned by whoever is holding the shaker.

name: Egg Drop Situation
description:
Egg poured in a thin ribbon into water hot enough to catch it on the way down.
Whether it becomes soup or wet egg depends entirely on your wrist.

name: Omelette du Roadside
description:
Folded once, badly, over whatever cheese was still in the bag.
French in ambition and roadside in execution.

name: Seared Meat
description:
Hot pan, dry surface, hands off.
This is less a recipe than the first thing anybody ever learns to do to an animal.

name: Backroad Skewers
description:
Cubes of whatever you killed threaded onto whatever you were carrying.
The vessel is structural here rather than decorative.

name: Mystery Meat Paste
description:
Not a meal, and never trying to be.
It goes into other things, it has never once apologised for existing, and yes, you may eat it with a spoon.

name: Roast of Indeterminate Origin
description:
Lidded, buried in vegetables, and left alone until the pot stops rattling.
Nobody at the table will ask what it was, which is precisely the point.

name: Flank on the Grate
description:
A big flat muscle over a hot grate, sliced against the grain.
Do it wrong and it is a shoe; do it right and it is a Tuesday you remember.

name: Charred Rack
description:
Bones on the outside so the fire has something to hold on to.
There is no dignified way to eat this and nobody has ever attempted one.

name: Rib Broth
description:
Bones, water, hours.
Half of everything else in the kitchen is downstream of this one pot.

name: Fried Wing Pile
description:
Twice through the oil, once to cook it and once for the crackle.
Portion control remains theoretically possible.

name: Steamed Wings
description:
Gentle heat renders the fat without picking a fight with the skin.
This is what you make when somebody in the party is ill.

name: Blood Pudding
description:
Set slowly over low heat until it will hold a spoon upright.
An acquired taste that most people acquire somewhere around the second bite.

name: Crimson Custard
description:
Steamed only until it barely sets, then eaten with a spoon.
Savoury, iron-bright, and far better than its colour has any right to suggest.

name: Heartpaccio
description:
Raw, cut fine, dressed with acid and left alone for five minutes.
Heart is the leanest muscle an animal owns and it tastes like the animal meant it.

name: Skewered Hearts
description:
Over coals, turned once, salted twice.
Street food in every city the party has ever walked through and cheap in all of them.

name: Gel Stock
description:
Melted down into a broth that sets again the moment it cools.
This is the base layer under half the fancy things you will ever make.

name: Erocian Pudding
description:
A single lump of gelatin boiled until it slumps and sets again, which is the whole recipe and the whole trick.
It is a delicacy in Erocia, it smells inexplicably of oranges, and it is the first thing anybody here will teach you to make.

name: Entire Steamed Fish
description:
A whole fish laid over aromatics with the lid on for ten minutes.
Serving it whole is a flex and everybody at the table knows it.

name: Fish Chowder
description:
Fish simmered so gently in milk that everything eventually agrees to be one thing.
Thicker than a soup, looser than a stew, better than either.

name: Sashimi
description:
No heat and nowhere to hide.
This dish is entirely a referendum on your knife and your fish.

name: Crisped Flank
description:
Sliced thin and fried hard until the fat renders out and what is left shatters between your fingers.
It gets scattered over other food and it has never once made anything worse.

name: Meatballs
description:
Bound with grain and egg, rolled between wet palms, browned all over and then finished in whatever sauce is going.
Rolling them all the same size is the only difficult part and nobody manages it.

name: Bearcat Burnt Ends
description:
The tips of the flank cut away, sauced, and returned to the coals until they candy.
The best part of the animal, and there are only ever four of them.

name: Beefy Tail Ragu
description:
Simmered until the meat gives up entirely and joins the sauce.
Traditionally served over anything that will hold still long enough.

name: Snooping Eyeball Bisque
description:
Blended smooth so that nothing left in the bowl can look back at you.
Rich, faintly briny, and best served to guests who did not ask what was in it.

name: Virgin Blood Sausage
description:
Bound with grain, cased, and steamed until it is firm all the way through.
Sliced thin it goes translucent at the edges, which is how you know it worked.

name: Cumin-Crusted Ribs
description:
Rubbed heavy, roasted low, and left until the crust is audible under a knife.
Smells like a market street two towns over from wherever you are.

name: Bone-Drunk Tofu
description:
Blocks of bean curd lowered into stock made from bones and left to drink until they come out heavier than they went in.
The one ingredient in this lane that never lived, doing a better impression of everything that did.

name: Second-Day Flank
description:
Yesterday's meat pressed back into a hot pan until the edges catch again, tossed through paste and hard cheese, then buried under
something peppery and something that shatters. It has no business being this good and everybody who makes it says so out loud.

name: Dargin Tail Braise
description:
Dragon-kin tail browned hard and drowned in stock for half a day, with allium at both ends of the process — caramelised into the pot
until it dissolves and goes black, then raw and green over the top at the last second.

name: Giga Flank Chateaubriand
description:
A cut this size demands a lidded pot and a certain amount of nerve.
Basted continuously in butter that was already cooked to hazelnut before it ever touched the meat.

name: Peerless Consomme
description:
Stock lifted clear twice through a raft of egg white, then let down with the clearest water the party is carrying.
It arrives looking like a glass of nothing and tastes like the sea's opinion of you.

name: Iridescent Confit
description:
The feathers still refract after cooking, which the kitchen has collectively decided is a feature.
Submerged entirely in rendered fat and held at a whisper for six hours.

name: Salt-Baked Sparkling Fish
description:
Encased in a shell of salt and egg white and baked until the crust rings when tapped, then opened over a pool of green.
Cracking it at the table is the entire reason to make it.

name: Ghosty Souffle
description:
Built on a sauce base, because loose cheese has never once risen.
It goes higher than it should and stays there longer than it should, and nobody has been comfortable with why.

name: Deathless Cut
description:
A heart too large to cook by any other means, buried for a day and a night in a pot lined with everything the kitchen knew how to
make, and finished with something raw and green. Eating it once permanently changes what your body believes it is capable of.

name: Full Circle
description:
The rack curls back onto itself and is grilled in a closed circle, painted the whole way round with a glaze of bitter chocolate and
chilli. The last bite tastes exactly like the first, which is either the spice or the point.

name: Stained Glass
description:
A single flawless gel set around flowers held in two states at once — fresh blossoms and candied petals, suspended apart by nothing
but stock and nerve. It holds its own weight, it holds the light, and it holds up under a spoon.

name: The Bare Blade
description:
One fish broken down into every cut it has, each piece dressed differently and finished with flakes that dissolve on contact.
There is nowhere to hide: each sauce sits alone beside a piece of raw fish and answers for itself.

name: Morning Porridge
description:
Cooked well past the point where the grain gives up its structure and turns into comfort.
Somebody in every party insists on making it wrong.

name: Toasted Grain
description:
Dry-toasted in a hot pan until it smells like a bakery and starts to pop.
Keeps for weeks and makes everything downstream of it taste deliberate.

name: Egg Fried Rice
description:
Yesterday's grain, today's pan, whatever else survived the week, and scallion thrown in at the very end so the whole thing does not
read as brown. The one dish that is better made with stale ingredients than fresh ones.

name: Smashed Potatoes
description:
Boiled soft and broken up by hand in the pot they cooked in, then enriched well past the point of good sense.
Never take a blade to them — it turns the starch to glue and there is no way back.

name: Roasted Tubers
description:
Cut into wedges, tossed in oil, and roasted until the outsides go rough and golden.
The inside is the reward and the outside is the reason.

name: Potato Crisps
description:
Sliced translucent and dropped into oil hot enough to seize them instantly.
Nobody has ever made exactly as many of these as they intended to.

name: Cold Potato Salad
description:
Dressed while still warm so it drinks everything, then chilled until the flavours settle down.
Improves overnight, which makes it the only dish here that rewards forgetting about it.

name: Toasted Nuts
description:
Shaken over medium heat until they colour and the whole room notices.
Thirty seconds separates perfect from ruined and the pan gives no warning.

name: Nut Butter
description:
Blended long past the point where it looks like it has failed, until it suddenly turns.
Patience is the entire recipe and the machine does the rest.

name: Candied Nuts
description:
Tossed in melting sugar until each one wears a shell that cracks.
Road food, party food, and the reason several characters have chipped teeth.

name: Noodles in Broth
description:
Noodles, hot liquid, something green, and no further ambition.
Eaten more often than any other dish in this document and never once photographed.

name: Cold Noodles
description:
Rinsed cold to stop them dead, then dressed sharp and eaten straight from the box.
The only correct food for a hot afternoon on a long road.

name: Griddle Cakes
description:
Batter dropped onto a hot dry surface and turned exactly once, at the moment the bubbles on top stop closing over.
Turning them twice is the mark of somebody nobody has told.

name: Toast
description:
Bread held over a live flame until it decides which side it prefers.
The simplest entry in this document and the one you will make most often.

name: Bread Pudding
description:
Stale bread drowned in custard and baked until the top sets and the middle does not.
Invented by somebody who refused to throw bread away and vindicated ever since.

name: Breadcrumbs
description:
Dried hard and then blitzed to gravel.
Not food, exactly, but the difference between a coating and a disappointment.

name: Panzanella
description:
Torn bread left to sit in oil and tomato until it softens without surrendering.
A salad that is mostly bread, which is the only kind worth eating.

name: Dumplings
description:
Wrapped, pleated badly, and steamed in a stack until translucent.
The first few are ugly and the last few are art, and they all taste the same.

name: Cheesy Noods
description:
Boiled, drained deliberately badly so a little of the water goes into the pan with them, then tossed until the sauce stops sliding
off. The starch in that water is the whole trick, which is why nobody who knows ever rinses them.

name: Savoury Congee
description:
Grain cooked in far too much water for far too long, until it bursts and the whole pot turns to silk.
It is what gets made for somebody who is ill, and what they ask for again once they are not.

name: Hella Loaded Baked Potato
description:
An hour in the pot and then split open while it is still steaming.
It is a meal by itself, which is the entire reason it grew that way.

name: Hazelnut Butter
description:
Toasted first, skinned badly, then blended until it goes glossy and dark.
Worth the extra step over any other nut and every baker in the world knows it.

name: Cooked Rice
description:
Rinsed until the water runs clear, measured exactly, and then left completely alone.
The hardest easy thing in the kitchen and nobody respects it until they get it wrong.

name: Spekkled Mac and Cheese
description:
Baked rather than stirred, because a crust is not optional, and built with three kinds of crunch — crumbs across the top, cracklings
over those, and a seam of pepper paste stirred through. This is the dish that ends the argument about which version is correct.

name: Whitecap Risotto
description:
Started in butter and then stirred continuously while the liquid goes in a ladle at a time, for twenty unbroken minutes.
Whitecaps count as carb here, which the recipe finds funny and the eater does not care about.

name: Soba on Ice
description:
Rinsed under cold water until the noodles squeak, dressed barely, and finished with green cut so fine it is almost a powder.
Restraint is the technique and there is nothing else hiding in the bowl.

name: Walnut Loaf
description:
Dense, dark, and heavy enough to work as a doorstop by the third day, with a soaker of toasted grain worked through it.
Cut thin, toasted hard, it outlives every other bread in the bag.

name: Big Gratin
description:
The gratin taken seriously, with hard cheese grated into every single layer and a crumb crust over the top.
It comes out of the pot in one piece and is cut like a cake.

name: Proof
description:
A whole loaf built around its own filling and baked sealed, so that nothing inside is visible until somebody cuts it.
The proof is in that cut: either the layers are in there or you have made a very large roll.

name: Amber Bowl
description:
Thirty parcels in a stock cooked down with onions until it goes amber, finished at the table with butter cooked to hazelnut poured
over and a sheet of lace-thin cheese laid across the top. The broth took a day and the crisp survives about ninety seconds against it.

name: The Gift
description:
A tuber the size of a helmet, rubbed in dark fat and roasted for most of a day until the skin goes to armour, then split and loaded
until it overflows. Everything goes on it — cheese, onions, cracklings, yogurt, and a fistful of ao negi cut fine over the top.

name: Couronne
description:
Laminated dough coiled into a ring, filled with nut butter and cream and studded with candied citrus before it goes back for a second
bake. It takes two days and it is the only thing in this lane that is unambiguously showing off.

name: Wilted Greens
description:
Greens hit a hot pan and collapse to a quarter of their volume in under a minute.
Everyone underestimates how many they need and everyone is wrong about it exactly once.

name: Green Puree
description:
Blitzed to a smooth, aggressive green that stains everything it touches.
It goes under other food, over other food, and occasionally onto a wound.

name: Green Salad
description:
Torn rather than cut, dressed at the last possible moment, eaten immediately.
Everything about it is timing and none of it is technique.

name: Slaw
description:
Shredded fine and left to sit until it gives up its water and softens.
Better an hour later, which makes it the only salad worth making in advance.

name: Caramelised Onions
description:
Forty minutes of low heat and near-constant attention to turn something sharp into something sweet.
There is no faster version and every cook alive has gone looking for one.

name: Onion Rings
description:
Sliced thick, battered, and dropped into oil until they float and go gold.
The batter is a delivery mechanism and everybody involved knows it.

name: Roasted Carrots
description:
Roasted long enough that the sugars come out and the edges go dark.
Carrots are the only vegetable that improves the more you neglect them.

name: Carrot Puree
description:
Cooked soft and blended with enough butter to turn it glossy.
Orange, silky, and considerably more sophisticated than a carrot has any right to be.

name: Blistered Peppers
description:
Straight onto the grate until the skins blacken and lift away.
One in every handful is unreasonably hot and there is no way at all to tell which.

name: Stuffed Peppers
description:
Hollowed, packed, and baked until the pepper slumps and the filling sets.
Structurally a bowl that you are permitted to eat afterwards.

name: Pepper Paste
description:
Blended into a thick red paste that keeps for months and improves nearly everything.
A spoonful of it is the difference between a meal and a good meal.

name: Tomato Sauce
description:
Simmered slowly until the water leaves and what remains is dark and concentrated.
Half the dishes in this document would like a spoonful of it.

name: Tomato Salad
description:
Cut thick, salted early, and left alone to weep for ten minutes.
The liquid in the bottom of the bowl is the best part of it and should be drunk directly.

name: Bean Stew
description:
Cooked long and low in enough liquid to keep them covered, until the beans give up and what is left thickens itself.
Cheap, filling, and noticeably better on the second day.

name: Raw Sprouts
description:
Rinsed, dressed, and eaten within the hour before they turn.
Nothing is cooked and there is nothing to hide behind.

name: Vine Wraps
description:
Leaves off the trap-vines, softened over steam, and rolled tight around a filling.
The vine still twitches occasionally and the kitchen has collectively agreed to ignore it.

name: Candied Petals
description:
Painted with egg white, dusted in sugar, and set cold until they go rigid.
Half decoration and half confectionery, and entirely unnecessary, which is precisely the appeal.

name: Mushroom Broth
description:
Simmered until the liquid goes brown and savoury and tastes vaguely of meat.
It is the closest a vegetable ever comes to lying about what it is.

name: Stuffed Sponge
description:
Halved, hollowed, packed with crumbs and cheese and roasted until the shell slumps around whatever went inside it.
Anything hollow enough to fill is a bowl the moment you decide it is.

name: Vegetable Stock
description:
Everything slightly past its best, plus water, plus an hour of doing nothing.
The most useful thing anyone can make out of what they were about to throw away.

name: Wilted Emeralds
description:
The best greens on the roster given the simplest treatment available to anyone.
Anything more elaborate is an insult and the kitchen will say so out loud.

name: Kale Crisps
description:
Roasted flat until they shatter, then seasoned while still too hot to handle.
Kale is officially a bread ingredient, which nobody has ever satisfactorily explained.

name: Tropea Onion Soup
description:
The soup made with the onion that costs money, which turns out to matter enormously.
Sweeter, darker, and worth the difference on every single occasion.

name: Glazed Happiness
description:
Named optimistically and, unusually for this roster, accurately.
Eaten straight from the pan by people who claim they are only checking the seasoning.

name: Purple Goodness
description:
Slabs laid into fat hot enough to hurt, where they squeak, resist, and then all at once stop resisting.
It drinks every drop it is given and comes out silk, which is the only reason anybody forgives how much it drank.

name: Roasted Pumpkin
description:
Cut into wedges and roasted skin-on until the edges blacken and the flesh turns to sugar, with its own seeds toasted hard and thrown
back over the top. Nothing is wasted, and the best part is the part most people throw away.

name: Blistered Tofu
description:
Pressed dry and fried until the outside goes leathery and blistered, then hit with pepper paste while it is still spitting.
Bland by nature and belligerent by preparation.

name: Fungus Toss
description:
Torn rather than sliced, so the ragged edges catch the oil and crisp.
Maitake is the one mushroom that occasionally converts a skeptic.

name: Romaine Boats
description:
Whole leaves used as the plate, loaded with cracklings and thick yogurt and eaten entirely by hand.
Romaine counts as a vessel here, which is the roster making a joke that turns out to work.

name: Sour Sprout Salad
description:
Sprouts that arrive already sour, leaving the dressing with almost nothing to do.
Sharp enough to wake somebody up in the middle of a meal.

name: Citrus Coral
description:
Steamed gently and finished with citrus sharp enough to cut straight through the mineral.
The only preparation that makes coral taste deliberate rather than endured.

name: Crimson Heat
description:
The darkest tomato on the roster blended into the hottest paste in the kitchen.
Nobody has ever described the result as mild and nobody ever will.

name: Parmesan Maitake
description:
Roasted under a lid until the cheese fuses itself to the ragged edges.
This is the dish produced as evidence whenever the mushroom argument restarts.

name: Edible Kale
description:
Grilled hard over open flame with enough chilli to change its personality outright.
People who state confidently that they dislike kale have usually not met this one.

name: What the Ground Gave
description:
Everything finest the ground produced, laid raw across a sweep of its own greens blitzed to a sauce, with onions cooked down to jam
and toasted nuts scattered over the top. No heat ever touches the plate, which is exactly why there is nowhere on it to hide.

name: Turnabout Braise
description:
A vine that fought back, browned in dark fat and braised a full day in stock and onions until it surrenders, with something raw and
green over it. Eating a thing that tried to eat you first is a specific pleasure, and this dish is built around nothing else.

name: Ephemeral Bloom
description:
An entire bouquet cooked whole and served whole in a broth of very nearly nothing, with petals from the same flower candied and set
around it like frost. It is the most delicate thing anyone in this party has made and it survives exactly one trip across a room.

name: Kaleidoscope
description:
Every vegetable sliced to the same impossible thinness and stood on edge in a tight spiral over a base of pepper and tomato.
Cutting it open shows every layer it was built from, which is the only proof anyone gets that it took all day.

name: The Uncredited Root
description:
Roasted carrots laid over a puree of the same carrot, with onions cooked down for an hour into something nearly black and butter taken
all the way to hazelnut. It is named after the carrot, but the onion does half the work and the carrot has never once acknowledged it.

name: Fondue
description:
Melted slowly with liquid and something sharp, because cheese without acid seizes into rubber rather than melting.
Eaten communally, which is either intimate or a hygiene incident depending entirely on the party.

name: Grilled Cheese
description:
Butter on the outside, cheese on the inside, and patience over medium heat.
Rushing it produces a burnt sandwich with a cold middle, and everybody has made exactly one.

name: Cheese Sauce
description:
Melted into thickened milk until it pours smooth and coats the back of a spoon.
It goes over vegetables, over noodles, and over several things that did not ask for it.

name: Milk Pudding
description:
Grain cooked slowly in milk until it thickens itself and the spoon stands unaided.
Somebody's grandmother invented every version of this independently and all of them are correct.

name: Custard
description:
Steamed low until it sets to a wobble and then stopped immediately.
The line between custard and sweet scrambled egg is about ninety seconds wide.

name: Whipped Cream
description:
Beaten until it holds a peak and stopped precisely one stroke before it would not.
Everything about this recipe is knowing when to quit.

name: Ice Cream
description:
Churned while freezing so the ice never gets a chance to form properly.
Stop stirring for long enough and you have made a sweet brick instead.

name: Browned Butter
description:
Cooked past melted until the solids toast and the whole pan smells of hazelnuts.
Thirty seconds beyond that and it smells like a mistake instead.

name: Strained Yogurt
description:
Hung in cloth overnight until the liquid drains away and what remains will hold a shape.
Half the volume and twice the everything.

name: Yogurt Marinade
description:
Meat left sitting in seasoned yogurt overnight while the acid does quiet work on it.
Nothing else tenderises this gently or this thoroughly.

name: Dragon Juice Custard
description:
Steamed until it sets, and it sets considerably faster than it has any right to.
The tongue stays faintly warm a full minute afterwards for reasons nobody has chased down.

name: Bug Juice Ice Cream
description:
Churned cold into something pale green that tastes far better than its name suggests.
Every single person has to be told twice before they will try it.

name: Parmesan Crisps
description:
Grated into a dry pan in small piles and left alone until they fuse and go lacy.
Two ingredients, and one of them is arguably unnecessary.

name: Baked Brie
description:
Baked in its own rind until the centre gives up entirely and floods the plate when cut, then finished with jam and something toasted
while it is still moving. Timing it is guesswork and overshooting is barely even a problem.

name: Cheddar Soup
description:
Melted into thickened stock until it sits somewhere between a soup and a sauce, then buried under something crisp so there is one
thing in the bowl that is not soft. Deeply unfashionable and defended to the death by everyone who grew up on it.

name: Malk Shake
description:
The cheap milk, blended thick, and honestly rather better for it.
Nobody has ever ordered one ironically more than once.

name: Nutmeg Cream Sauce
description:
Nutmeg is the thing that stops a cream sauce tasting like warm paint.
Grate it in at the very end and never a moment before.

name: Kream Puffs
description:
Hollow shells baked until crisp and then filled only once completely cool.
Fill them warm and you have produced a bag of sweet soup.

name: Moo Juice Panna
description:
The richest ordinary milk set barely firm, turned out onto a cold plate and flooded with coulis so it sits in a ring of its own
colour. It should wobble alarmingly and it should not survive being carried far.

name: Collapsing Cream
description:
It whips in about four seconds and it collapses in about nine.
Everything about serving this is a logistics problem rather than a cooking one.

name: Cheesy Bread
description:
The youngest cheese and the oldest baked in the same dish, where one floods and one fuses.
They have nothing in common and the pot does not care.

name: Dragon Ice
description:
Churned hard and frozen harder, and still faintly warm on the way down.
The contradiction is the entire dessert and the kitchen has stopped apologising for it.

name: Patience Cheese
description:
The oldest cheese in the kitchen grated through crumbs and baked over the youngest until one fuses and the other floods, then finished
with jam and candied nuts. Nothing in it can be hurried, and every attempt to hurry it has produced something worse.

name: Slow Fire Cream
description:
Frozen hard, served frozen, and yet warm on the tongue a full minute after the last of it is gone, with caramel and candied peel set
through it so the cold has something to break against. The kitchen stopped trying to explain this and started charging for it instead.

name: Potted Gold
description:
Onions cooked down in the two richest fats until everything collapses into one dark spoonful, packed into a pot with cracklings
through it and sealed under a lid of its own set fat. It is barely a dish and almost entirely a decision, and it keeps for a month.

name: The Mother Culture
description:
Three generations of the same living culture fed and folded into one another across a week, then buried under compote and nuts toasted
hard enough to crack. It tastes powerfully of somewhere specific, and no two people have ever agreed on where.

name: Berry Bowl
description:
Berries, cream, sugar, and no further intervention of any kind whatsoever.
The entire skill lies in not doing anything else to them.

name: Berry Coulis
description:
Blended and pushed through cloth until it runs clean and glossy.
It goes over everything pale and makes all of it look deliberate.

name: Berry Compote
description:
Cooked down with sugar until the fruit slumps without entirely surrendering.
Somewhere short of jam and considerably more useful than jam.

name: Blistered Berries
description:
Thrown into a dry pan hot enough to pop the skins before the juice has time to run out of them.
Thirty seconds, no sugar, and they come out tasting more like themselves than they went in.

name: Tropical Smoothie
description:
Blended thick enough that it must be eaten with a spoon and drunk with a straw simultaneously.
A structural failure that absolutely everybody enjoys.

name: Tropical Salsa
description:
Diced small and hard, tossed with chilli and onion, and left twenty minutes to argue with itself.
Fruit that has decided to be savoury, which offends people right up until they taste it.

name: Citrus Juice
description:
Squeezed and strained and served before the bitterness in the pith catches up.
There is a window and it is roughly ten minutes wide.

name: Candied Peel
description:
Peel simmered in syrup until it turns translucent and stops being bitter.
It takes an entire day and produces about a handful.

name: Citrus Curd
description:
Cooked gently with egg and butter until it thickens into something between a custard and a sauce.
Overheat it and you have made citrus scrambled eggs.

name: Citrus Sorbet
description:
Frozen and churned with nothing rich in it at all, which is exactly why it tastes so loud.
Served between other things to reset the mouth.

name: Roasted Citrus
description:
Halved and roasted until the cut faces caramelise and go jammy.
Squeezed over other things afterwards, which was always the actual purpose.

name: Baked Orchard
description:
Cored, filled, and baked until the skins split and the insides turn to sauce.
The dish that smells better than it tastes, which in this lane is a high bar.

name: Orchard Pie
description:
Fruit under a lid of pastry, baked until the vents run and the top goes hard and gold.
There is a correct number of vents and nobody has ever known it.

name: Orchard Relish
description:
Cooked down with onion until the fruit gives up its shape and the whole pot goes sharp and dark.
It exists to sit beside something fatty and it has never been the wrong answer to one.

name: Fresh Melon
description:
Cut off the rind, cut into blocks, salted lightly, and left cold.
Salt on melon is not a mistake, and arguing about it is a rite of passage.

name: Melon Juice
description:
Blended and strained into something so pale it looks like water and tastes like summer.
It separates within the hour and must be drunk before it manages it.

name: Fruit Salad
description:
Everything in the bag, cut to the same size, tossed in acid so that nothing browns.
The most honest recipe in this lane and it requires nothing but a knife.

name: Fruit Jam
description:
Cooked with sugar until it sets on a cold plate and not one minute longer.
The test involves a saucer, something freezing, and a considerable amount of nerve.

name: Fruit Fool
description:
Fruit crushed rough and folded through whipped cream just enough to streak it, never enough to mix it.
Stirring it properly is the only way to ruin it and everyone is tempted.

name: Coconut Milk
description:
Grated flesh steeped in hot water and then wrung out through cloth.
It is the only milk in this entire document that never met an animal.

name: Banana Bread
description:
The blacker the banana the better the loaf, which makes this the only recipe that rewards neglect this directly, and the butter goes
in already cooked to hazelnut. Somebody in every party is quietly saving three bananas for exactly this.

name: Mango Sorbet
description:
Blended and frozen with barely anything added, because it needs barely anything, and loosened with coconut milk so it scoops instead
of shattering. Deep orange, faintly stringy, worth the mess.

name: Cherry Pie
description:
Pitted one at a time, which is the entire reason this is not made more often, and bulked out with compote so the filling sets instead
of flooding. It stains the pastry through, which is how you know it is right.

name: Grilled Watermelon
description:
Thick wedges over coals until they collapse into something dense and almost meaty, then scattered with cracklings while still too hot
to hold. Salt, fat and fruit is an old trick and it has never once stopped working.

name: Pomelo Salad
description:
Segments broken apart by hand into loose pink threads and tossed with cracklings and something crisp, so that every mouthful has three
separate textures in it. The pith is thick and getting rid of it is most of the work.

name: Green Papaya
description:
Shredded before it ripens, while it is still firm and faintly bitter.
An entirely different ingredient from the ripe version and better in every savoury context.

name: Currant Buns
description:
Studded through enriched dough with candied peel worked in beside them, then baked until the fruit catches at the surface.
The scorched currants on top are the best ones and the argument about them never ends.

name: Honeydew Granita
description:
Flesh and pressed juice frozen together and raked apart, so the same melon arrives as both shards and syrup.
Restrained to the point of seeming like a mistake, right up until it is not.

name: Apple Sauce
description:
Cooked to collapse and blended smooth, and sharper than any shop version because you choose the sugar.
It sits beside rich meat and pretends that is a coincidence.

name: Nutmeg Pear Poach
description:
Poached whole in syrup with the stems left on, until they turn translucent and stand upright on the plate.
Nutmeg and pear is one of those pairings nobody needed to discover twice.

name: Snowed Melon
description:
Juice pressed from the melon, frozen hard and shaved into drifts back over the flesh it came from, with sharp curd hidden underneath.
The two never meet until a spoon makes them, and the whole thing collapses about a minute after it arrives.

name: Steamed Coconut Pudding
description:
Coconut milk thickened with grain and steamed under a lid until it sets just firm enough to hold a spoonprint, with mango laid over
while it is still warm. The pudding declines to compete with the fruit, which is the only reason the fruit agrees to show up.

name: Cherry Trifle
description:
Bread soaked through with compote and layered wet with custard and cream, then left overnight until the layers stop being layers.
It is built cold and improves entirely by being ignored.

name: Citrus, Three Ways
description:
Raw segments, a spoonful of curd and a scatter of candied peel, so that the same fruit arrives sharp, rich and crunchy inside a single
mouthful. Nothing on the plate came from anywhere else.

name: Blistered Grapes
description:
Roasted hard until the grapes burst and the cheese fuses to the pan beneath them, then finished with butter cooked all the way to
hazelnut. An unlikely pairing that stops being unlikely after precisely one mouthful.

name: Pressed Watermelon
description:
Salted heavily and weighted for an hour until it surrenders its water and the flesh goes dense and almost meaty, then dressed with
juice at the last second. Somewhere in the second hour it stops tasting like melon and starts tasting like something else entirely.

name: Midsummer Frost
description:
Frozen flat and raked every twenty minutes for hours into shards so fine they are gone before they reach the back of the mouth, then
scattered with peel candied until it snaps. It tastes like the one afternoon a year when nothing hurts and nothing is owed to anybody.

name: Nightfall Preserve
description:
Compote cooked down a second time with fresh fruit and syrup across a full day, until it is nearly black and thick enough to stand a
spoon in. A single spoonful outlasts the meal it came with and most of the conversation after it.

name: Ninety Seconds
description:
Green papaya into screaming fat with chilli paste, finished with citrus and a fistful of nuts thrown in at the last possible moment.
It is named for exactly how long you have, and the kitchen keeps a bell for it.

name: Castaway Custard
description:
Milk pressed from the same coconut, set with fruit into a custard and baked back inside its own shell until the top blisters, then
hidden under a lid of hard caramel. It is absurd, it is enormous, and nobody has ever finished one without help.

name: Caramel
description:
Sugar cooked dry in a pan until it goes amber, stopped with fat before it goes black, and scattered with flakes while still moving.
The window between caramel and charcoal is about eight seconds wide, and the salt keeps the sweetness from being the only thing there.

name: Brittle
description:
Molten sugar poured flat over nuts and left to set into a single sheet.
Breaking it up is the best part and there is no wrong way to go about it.

name: Sugar Glass
description:
Boiled well past syrup with a squeeze of acid to stop it crystallising, then poured thin onto a cold surface where it sets clear and
lethal. It shatters into edible shards and every one of them is a hazard.

name: Sweet Dough Fry
description:
Dough dropped into hot oil and rolled in sugar the moment it comes back out.
Best eaten standing beside the pot with no plate involved at any stage.

name: Plain Cake
description:
Sugar, flour, egg, butter, and no cleverness whatsoever.
Every cake anybody makes is this one with something else added to it.

name: Slime Pudding
description:
Set cold into something that holds a shape and wobbles under the spoon.
This is the dish that convinced everybody slime was food, which took some considerable doing.

name: Boiled Slime Sweets
description:
Cooked hard, cooled fast, and cut into pieces that stick to teeth for hours afterwards.
Herb and spice rather than fruit, because a boiled sweet has to taste of something that survives the heat.

name: Slime Foam
description:
Whipped until it triples in volume and then holds a peak indefinitely.
Physically improbable and structurally load-bearing in half the desserts below it.

name: Melted Chocolate
description:
Melted slowly over the gentlest heat available and stirred until it turns glossy.
Rush it and it seizes into something grainy that no amount of stirring recovers.

name: Hot Chocolate
description:
Melted directly into hot milk rather than stirred in as a powder, which is the entire difference.
Thick enough that a spoon leaves a trail behind it.

name: Chocolate Cake
description:
Baked until the middle is barely set and the top has cracked all the way across.
Underbaking it slightly is not a mistake; it is the recipe.

name: Chocolate Truffles
description:
Rolled by hand into rough spheres and dusted before they have a chance to melt.
They are supposed to be ugly and the ugly ones genuinely taste better.

name: Chocolate Mousse
description:
Whipped and folded until it holds air, then set cold for several hours.
Folding too hard undoes every bit of the work in about ten seconds.

name: Snap Cookies
description:
Stiff dough rolled thin, chilled hard, and cut into whatever shape the kitchen owns a cutter for.
It snaps rather than bends, which is the entire difference and the reason it travels.

name: Shortbread
description:
Three ingredients, more butter than flour, and nothing in it that could rise even if asked.
Bake it pale — colour is a mistake here and nowhere else.

name: Drop Cookies
description:
Dropped in rough spoonfuls, studded with something that shatters, and pulled out while the middles still look wrong.
Everybody holds a fixed opinion about the correct degree of underdone and everybody is wrong except themselves.

name: Sweet Crumble
description:
Fruit under a rubble of butter, sugar and nuts, baked until the top golds and the bottom bubbles up the sides.
It is a pie for people who cannot make pastry.

name: Sandwich Cookies
description:
Two thin cookies with cream and jam pressed between them, left cold until the filling stops trying to escape out of the sides.
The correct ratio is more filling than anybody thinks is wise.

name: Rolled Sponge
description:
Baked flat and thin, turned out while still hot and rolled up inside cloth so it learns the shape before it cools.
Unroll it cold, fill it, roll it back — done in the wrong order it cracks the whole way down and there is no hiding that.

name: Syrup Cake
description:
Soaked in syrup while still hot from the pot so that it drinks the lot.
Dense, sticky, and impossible to slice cleanly with any knife.

name: Fudge
description:
Boiled to exactly one temperature and then beaten hard while it cools, which is what forces the crystals small enough to read as silk
instead of sand. Beat it a minute early and you have made grit that nobody will finish.

name: Nougat
description:
Foam beaten into boiling syrup until it stiffens past the point of pouring, then packed solid with nuts and pressed between sheets of
paper overnight. It pulls at teeth and nobody has ever stopped at one piece because of that.

name: Chocolate Dipped
description:
Anything dry enough to hold still, lowered into tempered chocolate and stood somewhere cold until the shell snaps under a thumb.
The dipping takes four minutes and deciding what to dip takes considerably longer.

name: Slime Cordial
description:
The cheapest slime on the roster boiled down with citrus until it is thin enough to drink and sweet enough to want to.
It is what gets poured when somebody asks for something cold and nobody wants to explain what is in it.

name: Bitter Drinking Chocolate
description:
Cacao melted down into cream with chilli and ground nut, which is how it was drunk for centuries before anybody thought to add sugar
to it. The oldest recipe in the lane and it tastes exactly that old.

name: Slime Under Snow
description:
Old slime set until it slices like glass, then buried under enough sugar to pass for snowfall, with a seam of sharp curd hidden
underneath it. The contrast is the whole dish and both halves are load-bearing.

name: Shattered Yuzu Ice
description:
Crystals crushed to gravel through the sharpest citrus in the kitchen and frozen until they fuse back into a sheet, so it cracks and
stings in the same mouthful. A palate cleanser that overcorrects magnificently.

name: Midnight Icebox Cake
description:
Severe cacao folded through sweetened cream and layered wet with biscuit overnight, until the biscuit stops being biscuit.
The cream stops it being punishing and the compote stops it being solemn.

name: The Notorious
description:
Cooked down with the darkest cacao in the kitchen until the smell reaches the floor above and everybody up there forms an opinion
about it. Nobody has ever been neutral, and the people who like it like it violently.

name: The Quiet Dark
description:
The two darkest cacaos melted down with browned butter and cream and a whisper of heat underneath, then scattered with nuts toasted
almost to burning. It is not sweet and it is not comforting, and people stop talking when they eat it.

name: Vindication Jelly
description:
Two slimes nobody would touch separately, set clear as window glass with sugar shards suspended through them and a layer of curd
beneath. This is the dish produced whenever somebody claims slime is not food, and it has never lost.

name: The Cathedral
description:
Sugar boiled hard, pulled, blown and assembled into a structure that has no business existing, with caramel run through the joints and
candied peel set into the panes. It takes a day, it survives exactly one carry, and it is eaten by being broken.

name: Crossfire Ice
description:
Heat, cold, mint, bitterness and burnt sugar set into one dish that cannot decide what it is doing to you.
Every mouthful contradicts the one before it and nobody puts the spoon down.
